name: LMC
quote: Keywords: galaxies: dwarf — galaxies: interactions — galaxies: Magellanic Clouds — galaxies: structure ... Finally, these advances will help improve our general understanding of galaxy dynamics and the morphological evolution of interacting dwarf galaxies, using the MCs as a prototype for an interacting/colliding pair of galaxies.
location: Keywords; Sect. 6.3 (Constraints on the LMC–SMC Evolution), final paragraph
reader_note: Full text read (arXiv PDF v2). Galaxy label used as established throughout (keywords; 'LMC disk'; 'Magellanic-type galaxies'). The paper describes disk, off-centred bar and spiral-arm morphology and notes such structures are 'common in Magellanic Irregulars' (Sect. 1), but offers this to explain the structures by tidal interaction, not as a ground for the kind. No ground for the kind stated: N. A lenient reader might read the morphology comparison as L.

name: SMC
quote: Two massive satellites — the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds — were omitted from our study due to their large sizes, which render them impractical for a program of this scope.
location: Sect. 2 (Observations and target selection); SMC also listed in Table 2 (tertiary sample, not analysed)
reader_note: Full text read (arXiv:1806.06891v1; arXiv page lists DOI 10.3847/1538-4357/aac16b, confirming it is ApJ 860, 66, 'A MegaCam Survey of Outer Halo Satellites. III'). The SMC is not analysed: it is called a 'massive satellite' and appears only in Table 2 with compiled literature parameters. The paper never states a kind for the SMC, galaxy or cluster, and gives no ground. Coded N (no ground; here not even the label). Not X: it neither calls the SMC a cluster nor concludes its kind is undetermined.

name: Cassiopeia II
quote: The dwarf galaxy sample we focus on here comprises all the dwarf spheroidal galaxies that fall in the PAndAS footprint, as seen in Figure 1: And I, ... and the latest PAndAS discovery Cas II/And XXX. ... Cas II is reasonably faint ([value]) and has a typical size for galaxies of this luminosity ([value]).
reader_note: Full text read (arXiv PDF). The dSph label is taken as given in the sample definition, but Sect. 4.23 explicitly compares Cas II with galaxies in size at its luminosity: a comparison with the known galaxy population in light/structure (L). Borderline: the comparison is stated, not framed as an argument for the kind; a stricter reader might code N. Magnitudes and radii replaced by [value] for caution (not forbidden quantities). The same section notes its distance and systemic velocity are close to NGC 147/185 ('likely ... the same group'); grouping, not a kind ground.

location: Sect. 3.2 (Membership of the M31 sub-group); Sect. 4 (discussion of Fig. 6, absolute magnitude vs half-light radius); Table 1 (type cE)
reader_note: Full text read (arXiv PDF v2). Catalogue of galaxies within 3 Mpc; M32 enters as a galaxy by catalogue inclusion with morphological type cE, no ground argued. Sect. 4 says the galaxies 'seem well separated from the (Galactic) globular clusters' in magnitude vs half-light radius, but singles out M32 as an outlier from that relation, so the size-luminosity comparison is not a ground for M32. Table 5 comment 'Likely significant age spread and gradients?' is a population note, not offered as a ground for the kind. Coded N.
